def broadcast {n : Nat} (a : Vector Int n) (shape : Vector Nat 2) : Matrix (shape[0]!) (shape[1]!) Int :=
  fun _i j =>
    if h : n = 0 then 0
    else a[j.val % n]'(Nat.mod_lt _ (Nat.pos_of_ne_zero h))

    (broadcast a shape).size = shape[0]! * shape[1]! := by
  rfl

theorem broadcast_elem {n : Nat} (a : Vector Int n) (shape : Vector Nat 2)
    (i : Fin (shape[0]!)) (j : Fin (shape[1]!)) (hn : n > 0) :
    broadcast a shape i j = a[j.val % n]'(Nat.mod_lt _ hn) := by
  simp [broadcast, Nat.pos_iff_ne_zero.mp hn]

    (i : Fin (shape[0]!)) (j : Fin (shape[1]!)) :

    broadcast a shape i1 j = broadcast a shape i2 j := by

    (j' : Fin (shape[1]!)) (hjj' : j'.val % n = j.val % n) :

  simp [broadcast, Nat.pos_iff_ne_zero.mp hn, hjj']

def reshape {n : Nat} (arr : Vector Int n) (shape : Vector Nat 2) : Matrix (if shape[0]! > 0 then shape[0]! else n / shape[1]!) (if shape[1]! > 0 then shape[1]! else n / shape[0]!) Int :=
  let rows := if shape[0]! > 0 then shape[0]! else n / shape[1]!
  let cols := if shape[1]! > 0 then shape[1]! else n / shape[0]!
  fun i j =>
    let idx := i.val * cols + j.val
    if h : idx < n then
      arr.get ⟨idx, h⟩
    else
      0

-- Specification 1: The matrix has the correct dimensions
theorem reshape_size {n : Nat} (arr : Vector Int n) (shape : Vector Nat 2) :
    (reshape arr shape).size =
    (if shape[0]! > 0 then shape[0]! else n / shape[1]!) *
    (if shape[1]! > 0 then shape[1]! else n / shape[0]!) := by
  unfold Matrix.size
  rfl

theorem reshape_get {n : Nat} (arr : Vector Int n) (shape : Vector Nat 2)

def shiftRightInt (x : Int) (n : Nat) : Int :=
  if x ≥ 0 then
    Int.ofNat (x.natAbs >>> n)
  else
    -(Int.ofNat (((-x).natAbs - 1) >>> n + 1))

def rightShift {n : Nat} (a : Vector Int n) (b : Vector Nat n)
  (h : ∀ i : Fin n, b[i] < 64) : Vector Int n :=
  Vector.ofFn (fun i => shiftRightInt a[i] b[i])

-- Specification: the i-th element of the result is shiftRightInt applied to a[i] and b[i]
theorem rightShift_spec {n : Nat} (a : Vector Int n) (b : Vector Nat n)
    (h : ∀ i : Fin n, b[i] < 64) (i : Fin n) :
    (rightShift a b h)[i] = shiftRightInt a[i] b[i] := by
  simp [rightShift, Vector.getElem_ofFn]

-- Specification: the length of the result is n
theorem rightShift_length {n : Nat} (a : Vector Int n) (b : Vector Nat n)
    (h : ∀ i : Fin n, b[i] < 64) :
    (rightShift a b h).toList.length = n := by
  simp [rightShift]

-- Specification: non-negative inputs shift right as natural numbers
theorem rightShift_nonneg {n : Nat} (a : Vector Int n) (b : Vector Nat n)
    (h : ∀ i : Fin n, b[i] < 64) (i : Fin n) (hi : 0 ≤ a[i]) :
    (rightShift a b h)[i] = Int.ofNat (a[i].natAbs >>> b[i]) := by
  simp [rightShift, Vector.getElem_ofFn, shiftRightInt]
  intro hlt
  exact absurd hi (Int.not_le.mpr hlt)

-- Specification: negative inputs shift right with sign extension
theorem rightShift_neg {n : Nat} (a : Vector Int n) (b : Vector Nat n)
    (h : ∀ i : Fin n, b[i] < 64) (i : Fin n) (hi : a[i] < 0) :
    (rightShift a b h)[i] = -(Int.ofNat (((-a[i]).natAbs - 1) >>> b[i] + 1)) := by
  simp [rightShift, Vector.getElem_ofFn, shiftRightInt]
  intro hge
  exact absurd hge (Int.not_le.mpr hi)

-- Specification: result as ofFn
theorem rightShift_ofFn {n : Nat} (a : Vector Int n) (b : Vector Nat n)
    (h : ∀ i : Fin n, b[i] < 64) :
    rightShift a b h = Vector.ofFn (fun i => shiftRightInt a[i] b[i]) := by
  rfl

def Matrix (m n : Nat) (α : Type) := Fin m → Fin n → α

instance {m n : Nat} {α : Type} [Inhabited α] : GetElem (Matrix m n α) (Nat × Nat) α (fun _ ij => ij.1 < m ∧ ij.2 < n) where
  getElem mat ij h := mat ⟨ij.1, h.1⟩ ⟨ij.2, h.2⟩

def Matrix.size {m n : Nat} {α : Type} (_ : Matrix m n α) : Nat := m * n

def tril {m n : Nat} (arr : Matrix m n Int) (k : Int) : Matrix m n Int :=
  fun i j => if (j : Int) - (i : Int) ≤ k then arr i j else 0

-- Specification 1: Elements where j - i ≤ k are preserved
theorem tril_keep {m n : Nat} (arr : Matrix m n Int) (k : Int) (i : Fin m) (j : Fin n)
    (h : (j : Int) - (i : Int) ≤ k) : tril arr k i j = arr i j := by
  unfold tril
  simp [h]

-- Specification 2: Elements where j - i > k are zeroed out
theorem tril_zero {m n : Nat} (arr : Matrix m n Int) (k : Int) (i : Fin m) (j : Fin n)
    (h : ¬ (j : Int) - (i : Int) ≤ k) : tril arr k i j = 0 := by
  unfold tril
  simp [h]

-- Specification 3: Monotonicity in k - larger k means at least as many elements kept
theorem tril_mono {m n : Nat} (arr : Matrix m n Int) (k1 k2 : Int) (hk : k1 ≤ k2)
    (i : Fin m) (j : Fin n) :
    tril arr k2 i j = arr i j ∨ tril arr k1 i j = 0 := by
  unfold tril
  by_cases h1 : (j : Int) - (i : Int) ≤ k1
  · left
    have h2 : (j : Int) - (i : Int) ≤ k2 := Int.le_trans h1 hk
    simp [h2]
  · right
    simp [h1]

-- Specification 4: tril with k = max Int keeps everything (practically, using a large k)
theorem tril_diagonal {m n : Nat} (arr : Matrix m n Int) (i : Fin m) (j : Fin n)
    (h : (j : Int) = (i : Int)) : tril arr 0 i j = arr i j := by
  unfold tril
  simp [h]

-- Specification 5: tril applied twice with same k is idempotent
theorem tril_idempotent {m n : Nat} (arr : Matrix m n Int) (k : Int) (i : Fin m) (j : Fin n) :
    tril (tril arr k) k i j = tril arr k i j := by
  unfold tril
  by_cases h : (j : Int) - (i : Int) ≤ k
  · simp [h]
  · simp [h]
